name.description: The workspace's name, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

slug.description: The workspace's slug: groups of lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by single hyphens, of at most 64 characters, and not a reserved word, or the answer is 422 slug_invalid; if another workspace has it, the answer is 409 slug_taken. Without it, the slug is derived from the name: its letters and digits in lowercase ASCII, without accents, each run of other characters a hyphen, cut to 64 characters, or workspace if the name has none. If another workspace has that slug, or it is a reserved word, -2, -3, and so on up to -10 is added, and after that a random suffix of 8 lowercase letters and digits.

post.description: Signs in with an account's email address and password, and starts a session, whose secret the Set-Cookie header gives the client, and whose CSRF token the body holds. The account's first sign-in also gives it its personal workspace, named after its display name, which it owns; GET /api/v1/workspaces lists it. An address of no account, a wrong password, and an account that cannot sign in, such as a suspended one, are all answered with 401 invalid_credentials, after the same work, so that the answer does not tell them apart. A request that a browser's Sec-Fetch-Site header says comes from another site, or from another origin of the same site, is answered with 403 csrf_failed; browsers send that header only to https URLs and to loopback addresses, such as localhost. After 10 failed sign-ins in a row with an email address, whether or not it belongs to an account, the address is locked for a minute, and each further failure, once a lock ends, locks it for twice as long as the lock before, up to 15 minutes: while it is locked, every sign-in with it is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is locked, even with the right password. A successful sign-in forgets the failures, and so do 24 hours without one. Signing in, registering, and changing a password share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering also has one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.description: Changes the signed-in account's password, if current_password is the account's, or the answer is 403 wrong_password. The new password must have at least 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points once it is in NFKC, and must not be one of the 10,000 most common passwords, or the answer is 422 weak_password. Changing it revokes every other session of the account, and gives the session of the request a new secret, in the Set-Cookie header, and a new CSRF token, in the body, so that the old ones are no longer valid. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. Signing in, registering, and changing a password share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering also has one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.description: Creates an account with an email address, a display name, and a password, if the instance's signup policy, STORYCREEP_SIGNUP, lets anyone register. Under closed the answer is 403 signup_closed, and under invite 403 invite_required, because only an invitation creates an account then; either comes whatever the request holds. An email address or a display name that its field does not allow is answered with 422 validation_failed. The password must have at least 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points once it is in NFKC, and must not be one of the 10,000 most common passwords, compared without regard to case, or the answer is 422 weak_password. Otherwise the answer is 202 without a body, whether or not the address has an account already, which then stays as it was, so that the answer does not tell whether an address has an account. Signing in, registering, and changing a password share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering also has one of 10 a minute for each email address, and changing a password one of 10 a minute for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

patch.description: Changes a workspace's name, slug, or default locale; a field that the body leaves out, or sets to null, stays as it is. Only an owner or an admin of the workspace may, and anyone else with a role in it is answered with 403 insufficient_role. A workspace that does not exist, or in which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member or is a guest, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. A name or a default locale that its field does not allow is answered with 422 validation_failed. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed.

parameters.description: The session's CSRF token, csrf_token, which signing in and GET /api/v1/auth/session return; without it the answer is 403 csrf_failed
